title.zh: 打的是備援，不是閘門：霍爾木茲真正的戰場在那條繞道上——而2019年被炸過的第8與第9號泵站，七年後又被同一種廉價無人機炸了一次
title.en: The target is the detour, not the gate: Hormuz's real battlefield is the bypass — and pump stations 8 and 9, hit in 2019, were hit again seven years later by the same class of cheap drone

focus.zh: 伊朗要的不是把海峽物理焊死，是要「通行需要德黑蘭同意」被承認——Iran與Oman那條七海里走廊爭的是authority不是access。只要有一桶油能不經它許可上市，這份權威就被貼現一次，所以最高價值的目標是備援而不是海峽。而備援的硬化成本是連續支出、價值只在危機那一刻兌現，於是沒人守：Petroline第8與第9號泵站2019/5被無人機打過，2026/9/10又被打了一次。戰爭險把這件事攤開了——霍爾木茲7.5%至10%船殼值，彎靠沙烏地西岸不穿海峽只要0.1%；被市場定價成安全的那一層，正是沒有人防守的那一層。真正完全沒有備援的是LNG，而台灣的LNG安全存量只有約12天。
focus.en: Iran does not need Hormuz welded shut; it needs passage to require Tehran's consent — the seven-mile corridor it negotiated with Oman is a fight about authority, not access. Every barrel that reaches market without that consent discounts the authority, which makes the bypass, not the strait, the highest-value target. Hardening a bypass is a continuous cost that pays out only in the crisis hour, so nobody pays it: Petroline pump stations 8 and 9 were hit by drones in May 2019 and hit again on 9/10. War-risk pricing lays it bare — 7.5–10% of hull value through Hormuz, 0.1% to load on Saudi Arabia's west coast without crossing a chokepoint. The layer the market prices as safe is the layer nobody defends. The cargo with no bypass at all is LNG, and Taiwan's LNG cover is about twelve days.

title.zh: 定價權移到了「修復進度」上：五天內四種互不相容的修復估計，Brent靠最不可查證的那一則跌了5美元——損壞可以從軌道看見，復原看不見
title.en: Pricing power moved to repair status: four incompatible repair estimates in five days, and Brent fell $5 on the least verifiable one — damage is visible from orbit, recovery is not

summary.zh: Petroline泵站9/10遇襲後五天內出現四種來源層級不同、彼此矛盾的修復估計：美國能源部長Chris Wright 9/15對CNBC說「以天計算」；Bloomberg引述未具名沙國與Aramco官員稱「數天內恢復約一半運能、完整修復約六週」；區域官員向Reuters一線媒體表示3至5週；而Lipow Oil Associates總裁Andy Lipow看過公開影像後估「需要數月」。9/18報告已記錄，把Brent從107.46美元打回102至103美元的，是這四者中最樂觀、也最無法查證的那一則（匿名官員口頭陳述），而不是外交或安全面的任何實質降溫。另一邊，損壞本身的公開查證能力其實很強：Copernicus Sentinel-3拍到Medina與Mahd Al-Dhahab之間的黑煙柱，NASA FIRMS偵到成團熱異常，Airbus、Planet Labs、MizarVision與Vantor的影像顯示兩座泵站有大面積火燒與結構破壞。能看見的是「燒過了」，看不見的是「換好了」——大型輸油泵與驅動機組的到料與試車無法從影像判讀。
summary.en: Within five days of the 9/10 strike, four mutually incompatible repair estimates circulated from four different tiers of source: US Energy Secretary Chris Wright told CNBC on 9/15 it was a matter of days; Bloomberg, citing unnamed Saudi and Aramco officials, reported about half of capacity back within days and full repair in roughly six weeks; regional officials briefed frontline wires put it at three to five weeks; and Andy Lipow of Lipow Oil Associates, reading public imagery, estimated months. As the 9/18報告 recorded, what pulled Brent from $107.46 back to $102–103 was the most optimistic and least verifiable of the four — an anonymous verbal claim — not any substantive easing on the diplomatic or security side. Meanwhile public verification of the damage itself is strong: Copernicus Sentinel-3 captured a black smoke plume between Medina and Mahd Al-Dhahab, NASA FIRMS detected clustered thermal anomalies, and Airbus, Planet Labs, MizarVision and Vantor imagery shows extensive burn and structural damage at two pump stations. What imagery shows is that it burned. What it cannot show is whether it has been replaced: delivery and commissioning of large mainline pumps and drivers do not read off a satellite picture.

implication.zh: 對做量化的人，這是一個結構性的、可重複出現的不對稱：在這類事件裡，價格的邊際資訊來源不是可查證的損壞影像，而是不可查證的修復口徑，而修復口徑由營運方與攻擊方共同掌握。這使兩件事同時成立——營運方有動機把修復說得比實情快（穩定買家與保險），攻擊方有動機讓外界相信修復很慢（維持風險溢價）。專業交易機構使用即時衛星監測的比例已從2015年的18%升到2024年的82%，也就是說「看得見的那一半」已經被定價完了，剩下的alpha全集中在看不見的那一半。對做provenance的人，這是一個現成的研究標的：同一實體事件的四條敘述鏈，來源層級、可驗證性與市場影響力完全不成正比——影響力最大的那一條可驗證性最低。
implication.en: For anyone running quant strategies this is a structural, repeatable asymmetry: in events like this the marginal price-setting information is not verifiable damage imagery but unverifiable repair guidance, and repair guidance is jointly held by the operator and the attacker. Both incentives point the same way — the operator wants repair to sound faster than it is, to hold buyers and insurers; the attacker wants it to sound slower, to preserve the risk premium. The share of professional trading firms using real-time satellite monitoring rose from 18% in 2015 to 82% in 2024, which means the visible half is already priced and the remaining alpha sits entirely in the invisible half. For provenance work this is a ready-made case: four narrative chains from one physical event, where source tier, verifiability and market impact are inversely related — the chain with the most impact has the least verifiability.

counterpoint.zh: 反方說法也成立：油價當週的回落可能主要不是那則管線消息，而是9/16 FOMC升息一碼後的需求端與美元效果，管線消息只是被事後拿來解釋走勢的敘事。要分辨得看盤中而非日線——若跌勢集中在Bloomberg那則報導發布後的數十分鐘內，因果站得住；若跌勢平均分布在升息後兩天，那我這條就是把市場的既有走勢誤讀成資訊事件。我目前沒有盤中數據，所以這條只能給likely。
counterpoint.en: The rebuttal holds too: that week's decline may owe less to the pipeline story than to demand-side and dollar effects after the 9/16 FOMC hike, with the pipeline line merely supplying a post-hoc narrative. Distinguishing them requires intraday rather than daily data — if the move clusters in the tens of minutes after the Bloomberg report, causation stands; if it spreads evenly across the two days after the hike, I have mistaken an existing trend for an information event. I do not have intraday data, so this item stays at likely.

items.source: CNBC（Chris Wright 9/15訪談）；Bloomberg（匿名沙國／Aramco官員，經Investing.com轉述）；Reuters（區域官員3-5週）；Lipow Oil Associates（Andy Lipow估數月）；Copernicus Sentinel-3／NASA FIRMS／Airbus／Planet Labs影像；9/18報告

title.zh: 同兩個節點、隔七年、同一種武器：2019/5被打的第8與第9號泵站，2026/9/10又被打了一次——不是沒人知道，是和平年度沒人有理由付這筆錢
title.en: Same two nodes, seven years apart, same class of weapon: pump stations 8 and 9, struck in May 2019, struck again on 9/10 — not an intelligence gap, a peacetime budget outcome

summary.zh: 沙烏地外交部聲明譴責「來自伊拉克的數架無人機」攻擊Riyadh與Madinah地區的東西輸油管線（Petroline），造成火災、設施損害與數人受傷；受損的是第8與第9號泵站，正是2019/5/14被胡塞無人機攻擊（即Afif攻擊）的同一組節點，當年8號站起火、輕微損壞，9號站同樣被鎖定。Petroline全長約1,200公里，自東部油田橫穿阿拉伯半島至紅海Yanbu港，2019年曾把緊急上限擴充到約7 mbd，戰爭期間實際承擔約4至5 mbd、即多數不經霍爾木茲的沙烏地出口。伊拉克方面的反應異常具體：政府承認攻擊源自本國境內、公開表示不接受國土被當作攻擊他國的「發射台」、宣布將對經證實涉入者採取法律行動；安全與情報聯合任務小組查獲並扣押一座據稱用於本次攻擊的無人機發射平台；總理Ali al-Zaidi改組邊境省份指揮體系，Maysan省作戰指揮官與省警察局長被解職，一批安全指揮官接受調查。
summary.en: The Saudi foreign ministry condemned an attack by "several drones coming from Iraq" on the East–West Crude Oil Pipeline (Petroline) in the Riyadh and Madinah regions, causing fires, facility damage and several injuries. The damaged nodes were pump stations 8 and 9 — the same pair struck by Houthi drones on 14 May 2019 in what is known as the Afif attack, when station 8 caught fire with minor damage and station 9 was likewise targeted. Petroline runs roughly 1,200 km from the eastern fields across the Arabian Peninsula to Yanbu on the Red Sea; its emergency ceiling was expanded to about 7 mb/d in 2019, and through the war it has carried some 4–5 mb/d, i.e. most Saudi exports that avoid Hormuz. Iraq's response was unusually concrete: the government conceded the attack originated on its soil, said publicly it does not accept its territory being used as a "launchpad" against any nation, and promised legal action against anyone proven involved; a joint intelligence and security task force located and seized a drone-launching platform allegedly used in the strike; and Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi reshuffled border-province command, dismissing the Maysan operations commander and provincial police chief with a group of security commanders under investigation.

implication.zh: 這條不是新聞價值，是機制價值：它證明備援的脆弱點不是資訊問題，是誘因問題。泵站位置公開、七年前已被實戰驗證為可打且有效，卻在七年裡沒被補強——因為硬化一條1,200公里、十餘座多為無人值守站點的管線，是一筆連續支出，而它的價值只在危機那一刻兌現。任何以年度預算為週期的組織都會系統性地低配這種支出。把這個結論搬到你熟的領域完全成立：企業的異地備援、備用憑證路徑、離線備份，全都是同一類「平時看不出報酬、危機時是全部」的資產，也因此全都是同一類最可能疏於防護的資產。第二個值得記的是巴格達的反應——代理人模式的核心資產是不可歸責性，而這次伊拉克用解職與查扣把歸責往自己身上拉，代表這項資產正在折舊。
implication.en: The value here is mechanistic, not newsworthy: it shows the bypass's weak point is an incentive problem, not an information problem. The pump stations' locations are public and were combat-proven as reachable and effective seven years ago, yet nothing was hardened — because hardening 1,200 km and a dozen-plus mostly unmanned sites is a continuous cost whose payoff lands only in the crisis hour. Any organisation budgeting annually will systematically underfund it. The conclusion transfers cleanly to your own domain: offsite failover, backup credential paths, offline backups are all assets that show no peacetime return and are everything in a crisis — and are therefore all in the same category of chronically under-defended. The second thing worth recording is Baghdad's reaction: non-attributability is the core asset of the proxy model, and Iraq just pulled attribution toward itself through dismissals and a seizure. That asset is depreciating.

items.source: 沙烏地外交部聲明；伊拉克政府聲明與人事處分；2019 Afif攻擊紀錄；經Al Jazeera／ABC News（Australia）／CNN／FDD's Long War Journal轉述

title.zh: 戰爭險把備援的真實價值攤開了：霍爾木茲7.5%-10%船殼值、Bab el-Mandeb約0.5%、彎靠沙烏地西岸不穿海峽只要0.1%——但這條0.1%的路對亞洲買家幾乎不存在
title.en: War-risk pricing lays the bypass bare: 7.5–10% of hull value through Hormuz, ~0.5% at Bab el-Mandeb, 0.1% to load on Saudi Arabia's west coast — and that 0.1% route barely exists for Asian buyers

summary.zh: 據Marsh、Lloyd's List等保險與航運市場來源，霍爾木茲航段的戰爭險附加費已達船殼值7.5%至10%（戰前約0.25%），單趟對一艘一億美元油輪意味300萬至1,000萬美元；Bab el-Mandeb約0.5%；而彎靠沙烏地西岸、不需穿越任何海峽的裝載約0.1%。也就是說，保險市場把Yanbu這條繞道定價成比霍爾木茲安全七十五到一百倍。但這個0.1%只對往北經Suez進地中海與大西洋盆地的貨有效：要把同一批油送到亞洲，得從Sohar做船對船轉載後西行穿直布羅陀、繞好望角，約13,140海里，相對霍爾木茲航線的約3,370海里，多出將近一個月航程與相應的噸位需求。Oman的Duqm港則被視為另一條可能的繞道出口。UAE端的ADCOP（Habshan至Fujairah）約1.5至1.8 mbd，2026年3月報導的利用率約71%、僅餘約44萬桶／日餘裕，而該餘裕反映的是Fujairah港的吞吐上限而非策略儲備；UAE正加速West-East 1管線，目標2027年把不經海峽的運能拉到約3.6 mbd。
summary.en: Per insurance and shipping market sources including Marsh and Lloyd's List, war-risk premiums on the Hormuz leg have reached 7.5–10% of hull value (about 0.25% pre-war) — $3–10 million per voyage for a $100 million tanker. Bab el-Mandeb runs about 0.5%, while loading on Saudi Arabia's west coast without crossing any chokepoint costs roughly 0.1%. The insurance market, in other words, prices the Yanbu route as 75 to 100 times safer than Hormuz. But that 0.1% applies only to cargo heading north through Suez into the Mediterranean and the Atlantic basin. Delivering the same barrels to Asia means ship-to-ship transfer off Sohar, then west through Gibraltar and around the Cape — about 13,140 nautical miles against roughly 3,370 via Hormuz, adding close to a month of voyage time and the tonnage demand that comes with it. Oman's Duqm port is viewed as another possible bypass outlet. On the UAE side, ADCOP (Habshan to Fujairah) carries about 1.5–1.8 mb/d; reporting in March 2026 put utilisation near 71% with only some 440,000 b/d of headroom, and that headroom reflects Fujairah's port throughput ceiling rather than strategic reserve. The UAE is accelerating its West-East 1 line, targeting about 3.6 mb/d of strait-free capacity by 2027.

implication.zh: 這條把「誰真的被備援保護到」講清楚了：繞道基礎設施在地理上是大西洋盆地的保險，不是亞洲的保險。對台灣、日本、韓國與中國，繞道能做的最多是把油送上市場、壓住全球價格，卻不能縮短自己的到貨鏈；而多出的一個月航程本身就是一次噸位需求衝擊，會透過運費而非油價傳導。實務含意有兩層：一，讀這類事件時，Brent的反應與台灣實際到貨成本的反應會脫鉤，後者要看運費與保費而不是油價；二，這也解釋了為什麼北京在9/18前後推動重開霍爾木茲——對亞洲買家來說，任何繞道方案都是四倍航程，重開海峽才是唯一真正的解方，這是德黑蘭手上最實在的一張牌。
implication.en: This clarifies who the bypass actually protects: bypass infrastructure is geographically insurance for the Atlantic basin, not for Asia. For Taiwan, Japan, Korea and China, the most it can do is put barrels on the market and cap the global price; it cannot shorten their own delivery chain, and the extra month of voyage is itself a tonnage-demand shock transmitted through freight rather than crude. Two practical consequences: first, when reading events like this, Brent's reaction decouples from Taiwan's actual landed cost, which tracks freight and insurance rather than the oil price; second, it explains why Beijing has been pushing to reopen Hormuz — for Asian buyers every bypass is a fourfold voyage, so reopening the strait is the only real fix, and that is the most substantive card Tehran holds.

counterpoint.zh: 反方：把保費價差當成「市場認為備援安全」的證據，可能是誤讀保險定價的邏輯。戰爭險定價主要反映船體與船員的損失機率，不反映陸上節點被攻擊的機率——0.1%只是說「這艘船在這段航程不太會被打」，並不代表市場相信Petroline不會被打。如果真是這樣，我「被定價成安全的那一層就是沒人守的那一層」這句話就只是文字上的漂亮，而不是一個機制。這個反駁我認為有相當份量；能分辨的是看沙烏地西岸裝載的保費在9/10之後有沒有動——若完全沒動，代表保險市場從頭到尾就沒在對陸上備援定價，那我這條的推論鏈斷一節。
counterpoint.en: The rebuttal: reading the premium spread as evidence that "the market thinks the bypass is safe" may misread how war-risk pricing works. It chiefly reflects the probability of loss to hull and crew, not the probability of a land node being struck — 0.1% says this ship is unlikely to be hit on this leg, not that the market believes Petroline will not be hit. If so, my line about the layer priced as safe being the layer nobody defends is rhetoric rather than mechanism. I take this rebuttal seriously; the discriminator is whether west-coast loading premiums moved at all after 9/10. If they did not budge, the insurance market was never pricing land-side redundancy and a link in my chain breaks.

items.source: Marsh（經S&P Global Commodity Insights轉述）；Lloyd's List；The National；Al Jazeera（9/17「From Yanbu to Sohar」路線追蹤）；Institute for Energy Research（UAE West-East 1）

title.zh: 真正沒有備援的那一層是LNG：Ras Laffan出來的每一立方公尺都必須走霍爾木茲，而台灣的LNG安全存量只有約12天——整場繞道辯論跟台灣真正的曝險無關
title.en: The layer with no redundancy at all is LNG: every cubic metre out of Ras Laffan must transit Hormuz, and Taiwan's LNG cover is about twelve days — the entire bypass debate misses Taiwan's actual exposure

summary.zh: 與原油不同，LNG沒有任何陸上繞道：Ras Laffan生產的每一立方公尺都必須經霍爾木茲出海，波斯灣內沒有任何能以有意義規模繞過海峽的液化或出口終端，而新建替代出口能力的資本規模以數千億美元計、時程以十年計。卡達與UAE合計約佔全球LNG出口兩成，IEA亦把海峽有效關閉的持續時間列為2026年全球天然氣需求的關鍵不確定性。台灣這一側的數字：2025年95%能源靠進口、油氣進口依賴度超過99%，約七成原油與超過38%的年度天然氣供給來自中東；原油戰略儲備法定90天、實際約140至150天，但LNG安全存量僅約12天，法定14天的目標要到2027年、靠CPC與台電把接收站與儲槽容量擴增後才到位，而卡達約佔台灣LNG進口三分之一。2026年4月已有報導指出，台灣為避開霍爾木茲而改由沙烏地紅海港口裝運原油——也就是說，台灣的原油對沖手段正是9/10被打掉的那條管線。
summary.en: Unlike crude, LNG has no overland bypass: every cubic metre produced at Ras Laffan must exit through Hormuz, there is no liquefaction or export terminal in the Gulf capable of bypassing the strait at meaningful scale, and building alternative export capacity runs to hundreds of billions of dollars over timelines measured in decades. Qatar and the UAE together are about a fifth of global LNG exports, and the IEA lists the duration of the strait's effective closure as a key uncertainty for 2026 global gas demand. On Taiwan's side: 95% of energy was imported in 2025, with oil and gas import dependence above 99%; roughly 70% of crude and over 38% of annual gas supply come from the Middle East. Strategic crude cover is 90 days by statute and about 140–150 days in practice — but LNG cover is only about 12 days, with the statutory 14 days arriving in 2027 once CPC and Taipower expand terminal and tank capacity, and Qatar supplies about a third of Taiwan's LNG. Reporting in April 2026 noted Taiwan had already shifted to loading crude at Saudi Red Sea ports to avoid Hormuz — meaning Taiwan's crude hedge is precisely the pipeline that was hit on 9/10.

implication.zh: 對你手上的台股部位，這條的可操作性高於任何油價判斷：台灣的原油端有140至150天緩衝，真正的斷點在電力端——12天的LNG存量、加上約三分之一來自一個完全無法繞道的來源。這意味著台灣對霍爾木茲的曝險不是「油價上漲」這種連續變數，而是「冬季尖峰缺氣」這種門檻事件，而門檻事件對電子製造業的衝擊不會體現在油價相關標的上，會體現在用電密集度與自備發電能力上。第二層含意更難看見：全球關於繞道的政策討論全都是原油討論，因為原油可以繞、可以被政策處理；LNG不能繞，所以它從討論裡消失了。當一項曝險因為無解而從議程上消失時，它不會因此變小——它只是不再被定價。
implication.en: For your Taiwan equity positions this is more actionable than any oil-price call: Taiwan has 140–150 days of crude buffer, so the real break point is on the power side — 12 days of LNG cover plus roughly a third of it from a source with no bypass whatsoever. Taiwan's Hormuz exposure is therefore not a continuous variable like a higher oil price but a threshold event, a winter-peak gas shortfall. Threshold events do not show up in oil-linked names; they show up in electricity intensity and in whether a firm has its own generation. The second-order implication is harder to see: the global policy conversation about bypasses is entirely a crude conversation, because crude can be rerouted and therefore addressed by policy. LNG cannot, so it dropped out of the conversation. An exposure that leaves the agenda because it has no solution does not get smaller — it just stops being priced.

counterpoint.zh: 反方：12天這個數字可能嚴重誤導。LNG的「安全存量」是接收站儲槽的週轉庫存，不是為斷供設計的戰備儲備，因此它從來不該被拿來跟原油的140天並列比較——它真正衡量的是「到港節奏中斷幾天會出問題」，而只要有船在路上、來源可替換（美國、澳洲、馬來西亞的現貨），12天的意義就完全不同。把12天講成「台灣只剩12天」是我這條最容易被反駁的地方。要分辨得看替換彈性而不是存量：卡達那三分之一在現貨市場上要多久、多貴才補得回來，以及台灣接收站在冬季尖峰有沒有多餘的卸收與氣化槽位去吃下臨時增加的船班——後者是實體瓶頸，比存量天數更能決定結果。
counterpoint.en: The rebuttal: the twelve-day figure may badly mislead. LNG "safety stock" is working inventory in terminal tanks, not a war reserve designed for supply loss, so it should never be set alongside crude's 140 days — it measures how many days of interrupted arrival cadence cause trouble, and with ships en route and substitutable sources (US, Australian, Malaysian spot) twelve days means something quite different. Framing it as "Taiwan has twelve days left" is the most easily rebutted line here. The discriminator is replacement elasticity, not stock: how long and how expensively Qatar's third can be covered on the spot market, and whether Taiwan's terminals have spare unloading and regasification slots at winter peak to absorb added cargoes. That physical bottleneck, not days of cover, decides the outcome.

items.source: Arab Reform Initiative（Hormuz Under Fire：LNG無繞道結構分析）；IEA（海峽關閉對2026年天然氣需求的不確定性、卡達與UAE佔全球LNG出口比重）；CSIS（The Iran Conflict Illuminates Taiwan's Unique Energy Security Challenge）；Atlantic Council（The Iran war tests Taiwan's energy resilience）；Global Taiwan Institute／中華經濟研究院（儲備天數）

title.zh: Yanbu港才是那道真正的閘：管線3/28衝上7 mbd，但終端實測只裝得出約4 mbd、戰時估約3 mbd——「移除全球4%供給」這個說法高估了泵站的邊際貢獻
title.en: Yanbu is the real gate: the pipeline hit 7 mb/d on 3/28 but the terminals load a tested ~4 mb/d, ~3 mb/d in wartime — the "4% of global supply removed" framing overstates the pump stations' marginal contribution

summary.zh: 據產業分析彙整，Petroline於2026/3/28達到7 mbd輸送量，但Yanbu兩座終端的名目裝載能力約4.5 mbd、實測約4 mbd，顧問機構Vortexa估戰時條件下約3 mbd；限制項是泊位數、儲槽容量、裝載臂排程與油輪調度等實體因素。2026年3月Yanbu完成47艘VLCC裝載，是戰前月均11至12艘的四倍，同月有68%抵港VLCC在錨地等待超過36小時。9月遇襲後Yanbu裝載暫停，庫存從7月約2,100萬桶降至9月中不到1,500萬桶，以3.5 mbd計約僅四天理論供給。媒體與航運界普遍以「威脅移除全球4%原油供給」描述本次事件，依據是被中斷的約4至5 mbd流量。須註明：本條的港口能力數字來自產業分析與顧問估算，非Aramco或沙烏地能源部的官方申報，我在本環境下無法取得一手文件核對，故confidence列為unverified。
summary.en: Per industry analysis, Petroline reached 7 mb/d of throughput on 28 March 2026, but Yanbu's two terminals have nominal loading capacity of about 4.5 mb/d, a tested figure near 4 mb/d, and on consultancy Vortexa's estimate roughly 3 mb/d under wartime conditions — constrained by berth count, tank capacity, loading-arm scheduling and tanker positioning. Yanbu completed 47 VLCC loadings in March 2026, four times the pre-war monthly average of 11–12, and that month 68% of arriving VLCCs waited over 36 hours at anchorage. After the September strike loadings were suspended and stocks fell from about 21 million barrels in July to under 15 million by mid-September — roughly four days of theoretical supply at 3.5 mb/d. Media and shipping coverage generally framed the event as threatening the loss of 4% of global crude supply, based on the 4–5 mb/d interrupted. To be explicit: the port-capacity numbers here come from industry analysis and consultancy estimates rather than Aramco or Saudi energy ministry filings, and I could not reach primary documents in this environment, so confidence is listed as unverified.

implication.zh: 這條是本期主判斷的內部剎車，也是最實用的一條：如果Yanbu本來就只出得了3到4 mbd，那泵站受損移除的邊際出口量遠小於「全球4%」，而4至5 mbd這個數字描述的是管線流量、不是實際出口量。對你估算價格衝擊時的直接用法是：不要用管線標稱運能當供給損失的分母，要用Yanbu的實際裝載艘數。更深一層的機制含意是，序列瓶頸系統裡真正該被硬化的節點，往往不是最容易被攻擊的那一個，而是最難擴充的那一個——這裡最難擴充的是泊位與儲槽，而攻擊者打的是最容易打的泵站。兩者剛好不重疊，於是防守方的錢與攻擊方的彈永遠花在不同地方。
implication.en: This item is the internal brake on this week's core call, and the most immediately useful one: if Yanbu could only export 3–4 mb/d anyway, the marginal export loss from the pump damage is far below 4% of global supply, and the 4–5 mb/d figure describes pipeline flow, not realised exports. The direct application when you size a price shock: do not use nameplate pipeline capacity as the denominator for supply loss, use actual loadings at Yanbu. The deeper mechanism is that in a serial-bottleneck system the node that most needs hardening is usually not the one easiest to attack but the one hardest to expand — here berths and tankage are hardest to expand, while the attacker hits the pump stations, which are easiest to hit. The two do not overlap, so defensive money and offensive ordnance are permanently spent in different places.

narrative.zh:
**上期推演校準**

9/14週報五條指標：三條未到期（Ascend 950DT報價、兩家韓廠中國廠許可12/31、TSMC與Nvidia口徑）；一條間接被補強——9/20報告顯示HBM短缺卡在良率與資質認證而非晶圓片數，支持我對CXMT約25%良率的保留；一條指標寫壞了——H200已出貨給約10家中企、每家上限75,000顆附15%抽成，方向就是放量，但我把監管許可與採購意願綁進同一條又沒定義閾值，答案出來也判不了。

真正被削弱的是歸因層。9/16報告記錄兩大廠2026年HBM售罄、庫存9/7跌破10天、HBM4每疊約550美元——正是我上期自己寫下的反駁。機制層（稅率由記憶體循環決定）站得住，歸因層（管制究竟貢獻多少）站不住。而我指定的判別法「看價差不看價格」，一週後才發現沒有公開數據可查：連續第二週設出不可測量的指標，9/7週報犯過同一個錯，把「可證偽」寫成了「理論上可證偽」。本期起每條指標綁一個有固定發布時間的公開來源。

**問題是什麼**

主流讀法是：伊朗封了霍爾木茲，沙烏地靠Petroline繞過去，繞道就是解方。9/10從伊拉克境內起飛的無人機打掉Petroline第8與第9號泵站之後，這個讀法要倒過來——繞道不是解方，繞道才是目標，而且是七年前就標記過、七年來沒補強的目標。

**機制怎麼運作**

第一層是目標選擇。Iran與Oman談的七海里走廊，爭的是authority不是access。伊朗不需要把海峽物理焊死，它要的是「通行需要德黑蘭同意」被承認；只要有一桶油能不經它許可上市，這份權威就被貼現一次。在這個算式裡，備援是負值。

第二層是備援的防禦經濟學。1,200公里、十餘座多為無人值守的泵站，位置固定而且公開。硬化是連續支出，兌現只在危機那一刻，平時每一輪預算都先砍它——這就是同一組節點在2019與2026各被打一次的原因：不是情報缺口，是誘因結果。

第三層是序列瓶頸。管線、Yanbu的裝載能力、出Yanbu之後的第二個海峽，三道閘串在一起。攻擊者不必關閉海峽，只要讓當下綁住的那一道保持綁住，成本低一到兩個數量級，也不觸發封海峽會觸發的那種反應。

**證據**

重複是最硬的一條：沙烏地外交部點名「來自伊拉克的數架無人機」，命中的正是2019年Afif攻擊的同一組泵站。戰爭險攤開了市場的判斷——霍爾木茲7.5%至10%船殼值、Bab el-Mandeb約0.5%、彎靠沙烏地西岸不穿任何海峽只要0.1%。但真正的閘是港口：管線3/28衝上7 mbd，Yanbu實測只裝得出約4 mbd、戰時估約3 mbd，庫存從7月約2,100萬桶掉到9月中不到1,500萬桶。完全沒有備援的那一層是LNG：Ras Laffan出來的每一立方公尺都必須走霍爾木茲。

**各方自己怎麼說**

德黑蘭：Araghchi在北京說已與Oman談定重開方案，Oman官方未確認；他同時講明「與Oman談判不等於海峽會重開」。敘事核心是主權與通行管理，不是封鎖。它最在意的是華府把通行說成國際公共財——那句話直接否定它要的authority。

利雅德：官方敘事只談無人機從哪來、打在哪裡。但同一個利雅德用最後一刻的修正案讓9/14的Salalah七方會談破局，理由是原措辭會固化一個它無法接受的「新現狀」。它最在意任何把德黑蘭的通行管理寫上紙面的文字。

巴格達：最尷尬也最誠實——承認攻擊出自本國領土、公開說不接受國土被當作「發射台」、查扣發射平台、解職Maysan作戰指揮官與省警察局長。它最在意的是代理人的不可歸責性開始反噬國家本身。

華府：能源部長Chris Wright 9/15說停擺「以天計算」；Atlantic Council的處方是繞過去、別硬闖。它最不願被追問的是：這份處方本身就是一份目標清單。

台北：沒有敘事。9/24川習會之前，台灣的能源曝險不在任何一份繞道方案裡。

**未來 3–6 個月的推演與觀察指標**

主判斷：三到六個月內攻擊會集中在備援與其港口端，不在海峽本身；值得注意的升級不是海峽再關一次，是Yanbu、Fujairah或Sohar出事。一、若10/22前Petroline未回到4 mbd以上（看Yanbu月度VLCC裝載艘數與Kpler、Vortexa出口追蹤），官方的「3-5週」與「六週」都錯、Lipow的「months」對；若10/1前就恢復，我「泵站是長前置期節點」的判斷要降級。二、11/30前ADCOP／Fujairah或Sohar的STS作業區若遭攻擊或未遂，主判斷成立；若攻擊全回到海峽內的船隻，主判斷錯。三、西岸裝載的0.1%若升破1%（Lloyd's List、Marsh的定期說法），代表市場已把備援重新定價成前線——最直接的證偽指標。四、卡達對亞洲的LNG若到12月仍未恢復，台灣約12天的存量會在冬季尖峰暴露；看經濟部能源署月報與CPC招標。五、10/27-28與12/8-9兩次FOMC：Brent回到107美元以上而聯準會仍續升，代表這條供給側衝擊已經進了政策反應函數。

**我可能錯在哪**

最可能錯的是把一次戰術機會當成戰略設計。從Maysan省起飛打沙烏地中部，可能只是因為那裡剛好有通路、剛好有人。9/16報告的Taeb事件是最強的反駁：若7月讓停火破局的攻擊真是強硬派教士在總統與IRGC統帥都不知情下自行下令，伊朗體系內的授權本身就是破碎的，「理性目標選擇」不成立，我看到的模式只是隨機落點被事後串成故事。

第二個錯藏在接縫：我拿「港口才是真正的閘」同時當證據與反證。若Yanbu本來只出得了3到4 mbd，泵站被炸移除的邊際出口量就遠小於「全球4%供給」那種說法。兩者可以同時為真（價值在於「不需德黑蘭許可」這個選項，不在流量），但這是本文最弱的一段接縫。

第三，本期所有一手頁面都被本執行環境的出網政策擋住，我只能靠搜尋摘要取得二手轉述，因此全部條目的confidence上限壓在likely、沒有一條confirmed。最後一點自我提醒：上期我說連續兩週把世界解釋成同一個「窗口」形狀很危險；本期我換了形狀，但換成一個同樣好用的形狀並不等於更正確。
narrative.en:
**Calibrating last week's forecasts**

Of the 9/14報告's five indicators: three are not yet due (Ascend 950DT pricing, the Korean makers' China-fab licences by 12/31, TSMC and Nvidia guidance); one was indirectly reinforced, since the 9/20報告 showed the HBM squeeze is bound by yield and qualification rather than wafer count, supporting my scepticism about CXMT's ~25% yield; and one was badly written. H200 shipments resumed to about ten Chinese firms, capped at 75,000 units each with a 15% revenue cut — the direction is clearly upward, but I had bundled regulatory permission and buyer willingness into one indicator with no threshold, so an answer arrived that I cannot score.

What actually weakened is the attribution layer. Samsung and SK hynix sold out 2026 HBM capacity, inventory fell below ten days on 9/7, HBM4 runs about $550 per stack — precisely the rebuttal I wrote against myself last week. The mechanism claim (the tax rate is set by the memory cycle, not by BIS) holds; the attribution claim does not. And my discriminating test — watch the spread, not the price — turned out to have no public data behind it. Two consecutive weeks of unmeasurable indicators, the same failure as 9/7週報: I wrote "falsifiable" when I meant "falsifiable in principle". From now on every indicator is tied to a public source with a fixed release date.

**The question**

The standard reading: Iran closed Hormuz, Saudi Arabia routes around via Petroline, so the bypass is the answer. After drones launched from Iraqi territory took out Petroline pump stations 8 and 9 on 9/10, that inverts. The bypass is not the answer; it is the target — flagged seven years ago and never hardened.

**The mechanism**

First, targeting logic. The seven-mile corridor Iran negotiated with Oman is a fight about authority, not access. Tehran does not need the strait welded shut; it needs passage to require Tehran's consent. Every barrel reaching market without that consent discounts the authority, so in this arithmetic the bypass carries negative value.

Second, the defence economics of redundancy. Twelve-hundred kilometres, a dozen-plus mostly unmanned pump stations, geographically fixed and publicly documented. Hardening is a continuous cost that pays out only in the crisis hour, so it loses every peacetime budget round. That is why the same pair of nodes was struck in 2019 and again in 2026: not an intelligence gap, an incentive outcome.

Third, serial bottlenecks. The pipeline, Yanbu's loading capacity, and the second strait beyond Yanbu sit in series. An attacker never has to close Hormuz — only keep whichever gate currently binds bound. One to two orders of magnitude cheaper, and it does not trigger the response closing a strait would.

**Evidence**

Repetition is the hardest datum: the Saudi foreign ministry named "several drones coming from Iraq", and the nodes hit were the same pump stations as the 2019 Afif attack. War-risk pricing exposes the market's judgement — 7.5–10% of hull value through Hormuz, about 0.5% at Bab el-Mandeb, and 0.1% to load on Saudi Arabia's west coast without crossing any chokepoint. But the real gate is the port: the pipeline hit 7 mb/d on 3/28, while Yanbu loads a tested ~4 mb/d and roughly 3 mb/d in wartime, with stocks down from about 21 million barrels in July to under 15 million by mid-September. The layer with no redundancy at all is LNG: every cubic metre out of Ras Laffan must transit Hormuz.

**How each side tells it**

Tehran: Araghchi said in Beijing that a reopening plan is agreed with Oman, which Muscat has not confirmed, while also stating that talks with Oman do not mean the strait reopens. The narrative is sovereignty and traffic management, not blockade. What Tehran minds most is Washington calling passage an international public good — that phrase denies exactly the authority it wants.

Riyadh: the official line covers only where the drones came from and what they hit. Yet the same Riyadh collapsed the 9/14 Salalah seven-party talks with last-minute amendments, on the grounds the draft would harden a "new status quo" it cannot accept. What it minds most is any text putting Tehran's traffic management on paper.

Baghdad: the most awkward and the most candid — it conceded the attack came from its own soil, said it will not accept its territory as a "launchpad", seized the launch platform, and dismissed the Maysan operations commander and provincial police chief. What Baghdad minds most is that proxy non-attributability has begun to cost the state itself.

Washington: Energy Secretary Chris Wright said on 9/15 the outage was a matter of days; the Atlantic Council prescribes building around the chokepoint rather than forcing it. What Washington would rather not be asked is that the prescription is itself a target list.

Taipei: no narrative at all. Ahead of the 9/24 Trump–Xi meeting, Taiwan's energy exposure appears in none of the bypass plans.

**Three-to-six-month outlook and indicators**

Core call: attacks concentrate on the bypass and its port end, not the strait. The escalation worth watching is not Hormuz closing again but an incident at Yanbu, Fujairah or Sohar. One: if Petroline is not back above 4 mb/d by 10/22 (monthly VLCC loadings at Yanbu, plus Kpler and Vortexa tracking), both official estimates were wrong and Lipow's "months" was right; if it recovers before 10/1, my "pump stations are long-lead nodes" claim needs downgrading. Two: an attack or attempt on ADCOP/Fujairah or the Sohar STS area before 11/30 confirms the call; if all attacks revert to vessels inside the strait, it fails. Three: west-coast loading premiums moving above 1% from 0.1% (Lloyd's List, Marsh) means the market has repriced the bypass as front line — the most direct falsification test here. Four: if Qatari LNG to Asia has not resumed by December, Taiwan's twelve days of cover is exposed at winter peak; watch MOEA Energy Administration monthlies and CPC tenders. Five: the 10/27-28 and 12/8-9 FOMC meetings — Brent back above $107 with the Fed still hiking means this shock has entered the reaction function.

**Where I am most likely wrong**

The likeliest error is mistaking a tactical opportunity for strategic design. Launching from Maysan against central Saudi Arabia may simply reflect available access and available people. The Taeb episode in the 9/16報告 is the strongest rebuttal: if the July attack that broke the ceasefire really was ordered by a hardline cleric without the president or the IRGC commander knowing, authorisation inside the Iranian system is fragmented, "rational target selection" does not hold, and the pattern I see is random impact points I strung into a story afterwards.

The second error sits in a seam: I use "the port is the real gate" as both evidence and rebuttal. If Yanbu could only move 3–4 mb/d anyway, the marginal export loss from the pump strike is far below the "4% of global supply" framing. Both can be true — the value lies in the option of not needing Tehran's permission, not in the flow — but it is the weakest joint here.

Third, every primary page was blocked by this environment's egress policy, so I worked from search summaries of secondary relays; confidence is capped at likely across all items, with nothing marked confirmed. One last note to self: last week I warned that explaining the world with the same "window" shape twice running was dangerous. I changed shapes — but swapping in an equally convenient shape is not the same as being right.
